title: Polling place accessibility checklist (federal base)
description: Route-ordered survey of a polling place against the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, following the structure of the U.S. Department of Justice ADA Checklist for Polling Places: parking, drop-off, the route to the entrance, the entrance, the interior route and the voting area. Each failed item carries an election-day fix.

sources.title: ADA Checklist for Polling Places
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division

sources.title: Help America Vote Act of 2002, §301(a)(3) — accessibility of voting systems

kit.name: Threshold ramp
kit.description: Rubber or aluminum mini-ramp for a raised threshold or lip of up to 2 inches. Choose the size that matches the measured rise.

kit.name: Portable ramp
kit.description: Folding aluminum ramp with edge protection, at least 36 inches wide, sized for a 1:12 slope (one foot of ramp per inch of rise). Ramps over a 6-inch rise need handrails on both sides.

kit.name: Traffic cone (28-inch)
kit.description: Marks temporary accessible spaces and access aisles, and makes protruding objects detectable by cane.

kit.name: Accessible parking sign on a portable stand
kit.description: International Symbol of Accessibility, with the bottom of the sign at least 60 inches above the ground.

kit.name: “Van Accessible” sign
kit.description: Mounted under the accessible parking sign at van-accessible spaces.

kit.name: “Accessible entrance” sign with arrow
kit.description: Directs voters from inaccessible entrances and along the route to the accessible entrance.

kit.name: “No parking — access aisle” sign
kit.description: Keeps access aisles and curb ramps clear of parked vehicles.

kit.name: Wireless doorbell
kit.description: Battery push-button at the entrance with the chime in the voting room.

kit.name: Door wedge
kit.description: Prop doors open only where fire code allows and with a poll worker assigned to monitor the door.

kit.name: Knob-to-lever adapter
kit.description: Clamps onto a round knob so the door can be opened without tight grasping or twisting.

kit.name: Ground marking tape (roll)
kit.description: High-visibility tape for temporary space and aisle lines.

kit.name: Roll-out pathway mat
kit.description: Firm, stable, slip-resistant surface at least 36 inches wide for crossing grass, gravel or mulch.

kit.name: Rubber mat or cover plate
kit.description: Covers gratings and gaps with openings wider than 1/2 inch.

kit.name: Height-adjustable table
kit.description: Work surface 28–34 inches high with at least 27 inches of knee clearance.

kit.name: Extension cord with cord cover
kit.description: Run cords along walls; use a cord cover wherever a cord crosses a route.

sections.title: Parking
sections.summary: Start where voters arrive by car. Count spaces, then measure the accessible spaces nearest the accessible entrance.

items.prompt: Is parking provided for voters at this site?
items.help: Include on-site lots and garages the facility offers to voters. On-street parking alone counts as “no”.

items.prompt: How many parking spaces are in the lot voters will use?
items.help: Count every space, including accessible ones. Pollramp uses this to work out how many accessible spaces are required.

items.prompt: How many accessible parking spaces are there?
items.help: Count spaces marked with the International Symbol of Accessibility that have an access aisle.

fix.summary: Create temporary accessible spaces closest to the accessible entrance, each with an access aisle marked by cones.
steps: Pick level spaces on the shortest route to the accessible entrance.
Combine two standard spaces into one accessible space and aisle.
Place a portable accessible parking sign at the head of each space.

public.label: Accessible parking
public.pass: {value} accessible parking spaces.
public.fixed: Temporary accessible parking spaces will be marked on election day.

items.prompt: How many of the accessible spaces are van-accessible?
items.help: A van-accessible space has a wider space or aisle and a “Van Accessible” sign. At least one in every six accessible spaces must be van-accessible.

fix.summary: Designate a van-accessible space with a 96-inch access aisle marked by cones.

public.label: Van-accessible parking
public.pass: {value} van-accessible parking spaces.
public.fixed: A van-accessible space will be marked on election day.

items.prompt: How wide is the narrowest accessible car space?
items.help: Measure from the center of one painted line to the center of the other.

fix.summary: Mark a wider temporary space with cones and tape, or combine two standard spaces.

items.prompt: How wide is the access aisle next to the accessible space?
items.help: The striped area beside the space where a voter unloads a wheelchair. Measure line center to line center.

fix.summary: Block the neighboring space with cones so the aisle is at least 60 inches wide.

items.prompt: How wide are the van space and its access aisle together?
items.help: Measure from the outer line of the van space to the outer line of its aisle. Both allowed layouts (132 in + 60 in, or 96 in + 96 in) add up to 192 inches.

fix.summary: Widen the aisle with cones by blocking the neighboring space.

items.prompt: Is the van-accessible space in a garage or under a roof or canopy?
What is the lowest vertical clearance on the way to and at the van space?
items.help: Measure from the ground to the lowest overhead obstruction: beams, pipes, signs or sprinklers.

fix.summary: Designate a temporary van-accessible space in an uncovered part of the lot.

items.prompt: What is the steepest slope across the accessible space and aisle?
items.help: Lay a digital level in the space and the aisle, both lengthwise and crosswise, and record the steepest reading.

fix.summary: Set up temporary accessible spaces in a level part of the lot near the accessible entrance.

items.prompt: Does every accessible space have a sign with the International Symbol of Accessibility?
items.help: Pavement markings alone are not enough; the sign must be posted at the head of the space.

fix.summary: Place a portable accessible parking sign at the head of each unsigned space.

items.prompt: How high is the bottom of the lowest accessible parking sign?
items.help: Measure from the ground to the bottom edge of the sign so it can be seen over a parked vehicle.

fix.summary: Use a portable sign stand that holds the sign at least 60 inches up.

items.prompt: Do the van-accessible spaces have a “Van Accessible” sign?

fix.summary: Add a “Van Accessible” sign under the accessible parking sign.

items.prompt: Are the accessible spaces on the shortest accessible route to the accessible entrance?

fix.summary: Mark temporary accessible spaces at the point of the lot closest to the accessible entrance.

sections.title: Passenger drop-off
sections.summary: Check the place where voters are dropped off by car, taxi or paratransit.

items.prompt: Is there a passenger drop-off area at this site?
items.help: A curbside loading zone, porte-cochère or marked drop-off lane.

items.prompt: How wide is the access aisle beside the drop-off space?
items.help: The aisle runs alongside the vehicle pull-up space, at the same level, so a voter can get out with a wheelchair or walker.

fix.summary: Mark a 60-inch access aisle beside the drop-off space with cones and a sign.

public.label: Drop-off area
public.pass: Accessible passenger drop-off area.
public.fixed: An accessible drop-off area will be marked on election day.

items.prompt: How long is the drop-off access aisle?
items.help: Measure along the curb. It must extend the full length of the vehicle pull-up space it serves.

fix.summary: Extend the aisle with cones to at least 20 feet.

items.prompt: What is the steepest slope of the drop-off space and aisle?

fix.summary: Move the drop-off point to a level stretch of curb near the accessible entrance.

items.prompt: Can a voter get from the drop-off aisle to the walkway without a step (curb ramp or level)?

fix.summary: Place a portable ramp sized to the curb height at the drop-off aisle.

items.prompt: How high is the curb at the drop-off?
items.help: Measure from the road surface to the top of the curb. Pollramp sizes the portable ramp from this.

sections.title: Route to the entrance
sections.summary: Walk from the accessible parking or drop-off to the accessible entrance, measuring the narrowest, steepest and roughest points.

items.prompt: What is the largest change in level along the route?
items.help: Find the tallest step, lip, raised paver or heaved sidewalk joint and measure its height. Enter 0 if the route is smooth.

fix.summary: Ramp over the change in level so the route is step-free.

structuralIf.summary: A rise over 30 inches needs a ramp with intermediate landings, which is not practical as a temporary fix. Use another route or entrance.

public.label: Route to the entrance
public.pass: Step-free route from parking to the entrance.
public.fixed: A portable ramp will provide a step-free route on election day.
public.fail: The route to the entrance has a step.

items.prompt: How wide is the route at its narrowest point?
items.help: Measure the clear walking width between obstructions such as planters, poles, signs and parked bikes.

fix.summary: Move planters, A-frame signs and other objects out of the route, or mark a wider alternate route with signs.

items.prompt: What is the walking surface along the route?

options.label: Firm pavers or brick, joints flush

fix.summary: Lay a roll-out pathway mat over loose or broken sections.

public.label: Walking surface
public.pass: Firm, paved walking surface.
public.fixed: A firm pathway mat will cover rough ground on election day.

items.prompt: What is the steepest slope in the direction of travel?
items.help: Anything steeper than 1:20 (5%) is a ramp and must also meet the ramp checks in the next section.

fix.summary: Use a gentler alternate route, or survey this segment as a ramp (handrails, landings, edge protection).

items.prompt: What is the steepest cross slope (side to side)?

fix.summary: A steep cross slope cannot be corrected on election day. Use an alternate route if one exists and report it to the facility for repair.

items.prompt: Are there gratings, gaps or grooves in the route wider than 1/2 inch?
items.help: Check storm drains, expansion joints, and the gap where a sidewalk meets a building.

fix.summary: Cover the opening with a rubber mat or cover plate secured flat to the ground.

items.prompt: Do any objects between 27 and 80 inches high stick out more than 4 inches into the route?
items.help: Wall-mounted fire extinguishers, signs, drinking fountains, open windows. A cane cannot detect these.

fix.summary: Place a cone under the object so it can be detected by cane, or remove the object for election day.

items.prompt: What is the lowest overhead clearance along the route?
items.help: Tree branches, awnings, the underside of stairs. Mark not applicable if nothing is overhead.

fix.summary: Trim branches before election day, or rope off and cone the area under the low clearance.

items.prompt: Are there signs directing voters to the accessible route and entrance?

options.label: Not needed — the main route is the accessible route

fix.summary: Post “Accessible entrance” signs with arrows at the parking area, the main entrance, and each turn.

sections.title: Curb ramps
sections.summary: Where the route crosses a curb, check the curb ramp.

items.prompt: Does the route cross a curb between parking or drop-off and the entrance?
Is there a curb ramp everywhere the route crosses a curb?

fix.summary: Place a portable ramp sized to the curb height where the route crosses the curb.

public.label: Curb ramps
public.pass: Curb ramps along the route.
public.fixed: A portable curb ramp will be in place on election day.

items.prompt: How high is the curb where a ramp is missing?
items.help: Measure from the street or lot surface to the top of the curb.

items.prompt: What is the running slope of the curb ramp?

fix.summary: Place a portable ramp with a 1:12 slope over the steep curb ramp.

kit.note: Size to the curb height (1 foot per inch of rise).

items.prompt: What is the slope of the curb ramp's side flares?
items.help: Only where pedestrians may walk across the flares.

fix.summary: Place cones on the flares so voters approach the ramp straight on.

items.prompt: How long is the level landing at the top of the curb ramp?

fix.summary: A short top landing cannot be extended on election day. Look for another curb ramp or route.

items.prompt: Is the curb ramp kept clear of parked cars and other obstructions?

fix.summary: Cone off and sign the area in front of the curb ramp; ask a poll worker to keep it clear.

sections.title: Ramps
sections.summary: Any part of the route steeper than 1:20 (5%) is a ramp. Measure the steepest run.

items.prompt: Is there a ramp on the route (any part steeper than 1:20, or 5%)?
What is the running slope of the steepest ramp run?
items.help: 1:12 equals 8.33%. Measure in several spots and record the steepest.

fix.summary: A ramp steeper than 1:12 cannot be corrected on election day. Use another entrance or a compliant portable ramp system.

public.label: Ramp
public.pass: A ramp with a gentle slope leads to the entrance.
public.fail: The ramp to the entrance is steep.

items.prompt: What is the steepest cross slope of the ramp?

fix.summary: Report the ramp's cross slope to the facility for repair; look for another route.

items.prompt: How wide is the ramp between handrails?

fix.summary: A narrow ramp cannot be widened on election day. Use another entrance.

items.prompt: What is the rise of the longest single ramp run?
items.help: Measure the height difference between the landings at the bottom and top of one run.

fix.summary: Ramp runs rising more than 30 inches need intermediate landings. Use another entrance.

items.prompt: Is there a level landing at least 60 inches long at the top and bottom of every run?

fix.summary: Keep landings clear of furniture, mats and signs; if a landing is simply too short, treat it as a structural barrier.
steps: Remove anything stored on the landing.
Make sure the door swing does not cross the landing.

items.prompt: Are there handrails on both sides of every run that rises more than 6 inches?

fix.summary: Missing handrails need a permanent fix. Consider another entrance or a portable ramp system with rails.

items.prompt: How high is the top of the handrail?
items.help: Measure vertically from the ramp surface to the top of the gripping surface.

fix.summary: Report the handrail height to the facility; it cannot be adjusted on election day.

items.prompt: Do the ramp and landings have edge protection (curb, rail or wall) wherever there is a drop-off at the side?

fix.summary: Edge protection must be added permanently. Use another entrance if the drop-off is dangerous.

items.prompt: Is the ramp surface firm, slip-resistant and free of debris, ice and loose mats?

fix.summary: Sweep the ramp on election morning and apply anti-slip tread tape.

sections.title: Accessible entrance
sections.summary: Measure the door voters with disabilities will use. Hold the door open at 90° for width measurements.

items.prompt: Is the accessible entrance the main entrance that other voters use?

public.label: Accessible entrance
public.pass: The main entrance is accessible.

items.prompt: Is there a sign at the main entrance pointing to the accessible entrance?

fix.summary: Post an “Accessible entrance” sign with an arrow at the main entrance.

items.prompt: Will the accessible entrance be unlocked and usable the entire time the polls are open?
items.help: Ask the facility contact. A locked side door with no way to call for help is a common election-day barrier.

fix.summary: Arrange to unlock the door for voting hours, and install a doorbell so voters can call a poll worker.

public.label: Entrance hours
public.pass: The accessible entrance is open while the polls are open.
public.fixed: Ring the doorbell at the accessible entrance and a poll worker will help.

items.prompt: What is the clear opening width of the entrance door?
items.help: Open the door to 90°. Measure from the face of the door to the stop on the opposite jamb. For double doors, measure the active leaf.

fix.summary: If it is a pair of doors, prop both leaves open with a poll worker monitoring; otherwise use another entrance at least 32 inches wide.

structuralIf.summary: A doorway this narrow cannot be made usable on election day. Use another entrance.

public.label: Entrance door
public.pass: The entrance door is at least 32 inches wide.
public.fixed: Both entrance doors will be propped open on election day.

items.prompt: How high is the threshold at the entrance door?
items.help: Measure from the floor or walk surface to the top of the threshold on the higher side. Enter 0 if there is none.

fix.summary: Place a threshold ramp matched to the measured height, and sign the accessible entrance.

structuralIf.summary: A change in level this large is a set of steps. Use another entrance.

public.label: Entrance threshold
public.pass: No raised threshold at the entrance.
public.fixed: A threshold ramp will be in place at the entrance on election day.

items.prompt: What kind of handle or opener is on the entrance door?
items.help: Hardware must work with one closed fist: no tight grasping, pinching or twisting.

fix.summary: Fit a knob-to-lever adapter, or prop the door open with a poll worker monitoring.

public.label: Door handle
public.pass: The door has a lever, push bar or automatic opener.
public.fixed: The door handle will be adapted or the door attended on election day.

items.prompt: How high is the door handle or opener button?
items.help: Measure from the floor to the center of the handle or button.

fix.summary: Prop the door open with a poll worker monitoring.

items.prompt: How much force does it take to open the entrance door?
items.help: Hook the gauge at the latch side and pull (or push) slowly at a right angle until the door starts to move. The 2010 Standards set 5 lbf for interior doors and leave exterior doors to local codes; Pollramp uses 5 lbf as the practical target because heavy doors are one of the most common election-day barriers.

fix.summary: Adjust the door closer before election day, or prop the door open with a poll worker monitoring.

public.label: Door opening
public.pass: The entrance door opens with light force.
public.fixed: The entrance door will be held open or attended on election day.

items.prompt: How long does the door take to close from fully open (90°) to about 12° from closed?
items.help: Open the door to 90°, let go, and time it.

fix.summary: Ask the facility to slow the closer, or prop the door open with a poll worker monitoring.

items.prompt: On the pull side, is there a clear, level space at least 18 inches wide beside the latch edge of the door?
items.help: A wheelchair user needs room beside the latch to pull the door open without the door hitting their footrests.

fix.summary: Move planters, trash cans or furniture away from the latch side; otherwise prop the door open with a poll worker monitoring.

items.prompt: If there are two doors in a row (a vestibule), is the space between them at least 48 inches plus the width of any door swinging into it?

options.label: No, the space is too small

fix.summary: Prop the outer door open with a poll worker monitoring so voters deal with one door at a time.

sections.title: Interior route
sections.summary: Walk from the entrance to the voting room. Check hallways, inner doors and the way between floors.

items.prompt: How wide is the hallway at its narrowest point between the entrance and the voting room?

fix.summary: Move tables, trash cans, coat racks and stored items out of the hallway for election day.

public.label: Hallways
public.pass: Hallways to the voting room are at least 36 inches wide.

items.prompt: What is the largest change in level inside, between the entrance and the voting room?
items.help: Raised thresholds, floor transitions, a single step. Enter 0 if the route is level.

fix.summary: Ramp over the change in level.

structuralIf.summary: A rise this large needs an elevator or lift. Move the voting area to the entrance level.

items.prompt: Do any objects between 27 and 80 inches high stick out more than 4 inches into the hallway?

fix.summary: Place a cone or chair under the object so a cane can detect it.

items.prompt: What is the clear width of the narrowest interior door on the route?
items.help: Measure with the door open 90°. Mark not applicable if there are no interior doors.

fix.summary: Prop interior doors fully open (or open both leaves) for election day.

structuralIf.summary: This doorway is too narrow to use. Choose a different voting room or route.

items.prompt: How much force does it take to open the heaviest interior door on the route?

fix.summary: Prop interior doors open for the day (fire doors only with magnetic hold-opens or a monitor).

items.prompt: Is the voting room on the same floor as the accessible entrance?

public.label: Voting floor
public.pass: Voting is on the same floor as the accessible entrance.

items.prompt: Is there an elevator or platform lift voters can use without help?

fix.summary: Move the voting area to the floor of the accessible entrance.

public.label: Elevator
public.pass: An elevator serves the voting floor.
public.fixed: Voting will be moved to the entrance level on election day.

items.prompt: How wide is the elevator door opening?

fix.summary: Move the voting area to the floor of the accessible entrance.

items.prompt: How high is the highest elevator call or floor button a voter must press?

fix.summary: Station a poll worker at the elevator to operate it for voters who ask.

items.prompt: Does the elevator work without a key or staff override?

fix.summary: Get the key from the facility and keep a poll worker with it at the elevator all day.

sections.title: Voting area
sections.summary: Check the room as it will be set up on election day: check-in, aisles, booths and the accessible voting system.

items.prompt: How wide is the narrowest aisle between check-in, booths and the ballot scanner?
items.help: Measure with tables and booths where they will be on election day, including where the line will form.

fix.summary: Re-arrange tables and booths to keep 36-inch aisles. Include the layout in the poll-worker setup sheet.

public.label: Inside the voting room
public.pass: Aisles in the voting room are wide enough for a wheelchair.

items.prompt: Is there a clear space at least 60 inches across for a wheelchair to turn, including at check-in and at the accessible booth?

fix.summary: Move booths and tables to open a 5-foot turning circle at check-in and at the accessible booth.

items.prompt: How high is the check-in table where voters sign?

fix.summary: Use a height-adjustable table for check-in, or provide a clipboard at a lower table.

items.prompt: Will an accessible voting system (with audio, large print and tactile controls) be set up, powered and tested before polls open?

fix.summary: Add the accessible voting system to the delivery list, with power, and test it during setup.

public.label: Accessible voting system
public.pass: An accessible voting system with audio, large print and tactile controls.

items.prompt: Is there a clear floor space at least 30 by 48 inches in front of the accessible voting system?

fix.summary: Remove the chair and move nearby booths to clear a 30-by-48-inch space.

items.prompt: How high is the table surface of the accessible voting station?

fix.summary: Use a height-adjustable table for the accessible voting station.

items.prompt: How much knee clearance is under the accessible voting station?
items.help: Measure from the floor to the underside of the table apron.

fix.summary: Use a table with at least 27 inches of knee clearance.

items.prompt: How high is the highest control or ballot slot a voter must reach (including the scanner)?

fix.summary: Lower the scanner or place it on a table so its slot is within 15–48 inches.

items.prompt: Can a seated voter mark a ballot privately, out of view of others?

fix.summary: Turn the accessible station toward a wall and add a privacy screen.

items.prompt: Are power cords kept out of the route, or covered with a cord cover?

fix.summary: Run cords along walls and use a cord cover where a cord must cross a route.

items.prompt: Are chairs available for voters who cannot stand in line?

fix.summary: Bring folding chairs and place them along the line.

public.label: Seating
public.pass: Chairs for voters who need to sit while waiting.
public.fixed: Chairs will be available for voters who need to sit while waiting.

references: DOJ ADA Checklist for Polling Places — voting area

items.prompt: Is the lighting bright enough to read a ballot at every booth?

fix.summary: Bring battery work lights for dim booths.

references: DOJ ADA Checklist for Polling Places — voting area

items.prompt: Are magnifiers and pen grips available at the booths?

fix.summary: Add magnifying sheets and pen grips to the supply bag.

public.label: Voting aids
public.pass: Magnifiers and pen grips at the voting booths.
public.fixed: Magnifiers and pen grips will be at the voting booths.

references: DOJ ADA Checklist for Polling Places — voting area
